title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 9

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the record-review lesson take place?
tasks.audioText: The aviation documentation tutor will review a sample maintenance record on Wednesday at ten. Students should bring the task card and the component history extract. The class will identify the aircraft or component reference, task status and supporting document references. The tutor will explain how accurate records support continuity between maintenance teams.
options: On Wednesday at ten
On Wednesday at nine
On Thursday at ten
On Wednesday at eleven

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which history document should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The aviation documentation tutor will review a sample maintenance record on Wednesday at ten. Students should bring the task card and the component history extract. The class will identify the aircraft or component reference, task status and supporting document references. The tutor will explain how accurate records support continuity between maintenance teams.
options: The aircraft identification record and parts catalogue
The task card and component history extract
The maintenance schedule and defect report
The inspection checklist and release certificate

tasks.prompt: A maintenance record should make it possible to identify the relevant aircraft or component, the task performed and the supporting documentation. Entries should be clear, dated and attributable to the authorised person or process. If a task remains incomplete, its status should be recorded accurately. This allows the next team to understand what has been done and what still requires action. Reading 1. Which information helps identify a maintenance record?
options: Supplier contact details, purchase price and delivery date
Name of the training room, lesson time and group number
Aircraft or component reference, task performed and supporting documentation
Staff rota, annual leave dates and shift preference

tasks.prompt: Why should an incomplete task be recorded accurately?
options: So the next team can assume the task was not started
So the previous team can remove the original record
So the task can be marked complete without further evidence
So the next team understands what remains to be done

tasks.prompt: The task status ___ accurately in the maintenance record.
options: must be recorded
must record
recording
are recorded

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO details that support maintenance-record traceability.
options: An unrelated personal comment
An unverified assumption
Aircraft or component reference
Supporting document reference

tasks.prompt: The ability to follow a component or task through documented records is ___.
A task is not complete, but the record shows it as finished. What should you do?
options: Leave it because the record is already signed.
Raise the discrepancy through the approved record-correction process.
Delete the task reference.
Change the status without approval.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of aviation maintenance records in a logical order.
options: Record the actual task status
Identify the aircraft or component
Ensure the entry is attributable and traceable
Confirm the task reference and supporting data
correctOrder: Confirm the task reference and supporting data
Ensure the entry is attributable and traceable

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words explaining how maintenance records support continuity, traceability and clear task status between teams.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total. Score each criterion 0–2: (1) Record content — 2: explains how records capture completed work, current status and outstanding actions; 1: partial; 0: absent. (2) Continuity — 2: explains how consistent entries support the next team and avoid gaps or duplication; 1: partial; 0: absent. (3) Traceability — 2: identifies dates, references, responsible persons and links to controlled records as relevant; 1: partial; 0: absent. (4) English — 2: clear explanation and accurate maintenance-record vocabulary; 1: errors but meaning clear; 0: meaning frequently unclear.
